question.problem: The vector-valued function $r(x,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [\frac{1}{2},1].$ Which of the following could be $r?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284071/assets/56a380b075d10862170ed9c9a45c07dddff3eaef1ea9fb3109a61cc3d27b5ac4.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [a,b]$ has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(x)=\frac{1}{x}\ge 0$ for all $x\in [\frac{1}{2},1].$  

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{x},\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{x}⟩,\,x\in [\frac{1}{2},1],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
